question:
Select the most appropriate antonym to substitute the bracketed word in the given sentence.

An (unsullied) safety record swelled pride in Concorde's technical achievement as the years passed.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Tarnished.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Unsullied" means spotless, unspoiled, not damaged or stained. (बेदाग़, निष्कलंक)

• Its antonym (opposite) is "Tarnished", which means stained, spoilt, damaged in reputation. (कलंकित, धूमिल)

◦ Correct: An tarnished/stained safety record would be one damaged by accidents, the opposite of an unsullied one.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Undefiled" means pure, unpolluted — a synonym of unsullied, not an antonym.

• Option 2 "Impeccable" means flawless, faultless — again a synonym.

• Option 4 "Perfect" means without any fault — a synonym as well.

NOTE

• In an antonym question, first fix the meaning of the key word, then reject all options carrying the same sense. Here three options are positive words; only "tarnished" is negative.

• Word family: sully (verb — to stain), sullied, unsullied. Related antonyms of unsullied: soiled, blemished, sullied, defiled, besmirched.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

Training your dog have required a lot of patience.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. requires a lot.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence is the gerund phrase "Training your dog". A gerund (verb + ing used as a noun) is always treated as a singular subject, so it takes the singular verb "requires".

• The sentence states a general truth, so the simple present tense is required, not the present perfect "have required".

• "a lot of patience" is the correct quantifier phrase with the uncountable noun "patience".

◦ Correct: Training your dog requires a lot of patience.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "require the lot" is wrong twice — plural verb "require" with a singular subject, and "the lot" instead of "a lot".

• Option 3 "required lot" wrongly uses the past tense and drops the article "a".

• Option 4 "No improvement" cannot be chosen because "have required" is clearly ungrammatical here.

NOTE

• Rule: Gerund/Infinitive as subject → singular verb. Examples: "Swimming is good exercise", "Reading books helps you learn", "To err is human".

• "a lot of" is used with both countable and uncountable nouns: a lot of books, a lot of patience.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The question is why an ______ Hollywood film should provoke such a hostile reaction.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. innocuous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Innocuous" means harmless, inoffensive, not likely to upset anyone. (हानिरहित)

• The sentence contrasts a harmless film with the "hostile reaction" it provoked — the contrast makes "innocuous" the only logical fit. The article "an" before the blank also requires a word beginning with a vowel sound, which suits "innocuous".

◦ Correct: The question is why an innocuous Hollywood film should provoke such a hostile reaction.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "elicit" is a verb meaning to draw out (a response); an adjective is needed before the noun "film".

• Option 3 "obstinate" means stubborn — used for people, not for a film, and it gives no contrast with "hostile".

• Option 4 "erroneous" means mistaken or incorrect; a film being incorrect does not explain the surprise expressed by "why ... should provoke".

NOTE

• Watch the article: "an" signals a vowel sound (an hour, an umbrella), "a" a consonant sound (a university, a European).

• Synonyms of innocuous: harmless, benign, inoffensive, bland. Antonyms: harmful, noxious, offensive.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The respondents were very agile and ______ in subduing the situation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. quick.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is joined to "agile" by "and", so the two adjectives must carry a similar, positive sense (parallel meaning). "Agile" means nimble and quick-moving, so "quick" fits perfectly. (तेज़, फुर्तीला)

◦ Correct: The respondents were very agile and quick in subduing the situation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "hassled" means troubled or harassed — a negative word that does not pair with "agile".

• Option 3 "tedious" means boring and slow — the opposite of agile.

• Option 4 "tasty" refers to food and is completely irrelevant to people subduing a situation.

NOTE

• When two adjectives are joined by "and", they normally reinforce each other. Spot the clue word ("agile") and pick its companion, not its opposite.

• "Subdue" = to bring under control, to overpower. (काबू में करना)

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the bracketed idiom in the given sentence.

The last observation of yours has (hit the nail on the head).
option_1: To have no idea about anything
option_2: A personal interest in the matter
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Find exactly the right answer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "hit the nail on the head" means to say or do exactly the right thing; to describe a situation with complete accuracy. (बिल्कुल सही बात कहना)

◦ Correct: The last observation of yours has hit the nail on the head — i.e. it was exactly right.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "To have no idea about anything" is the very opposite of the idiom's meaning.

• Option 2 "A personal interest in the matter" corresponds to idioms like "to have an axe to grind".

• Option 3 "To hear rumours" corresponds to "to hear it on the grapevine".

NOTE

• Related idioms often asked in SSC: "hit the jackpot" (win big), "hit below the belt" (act unfairly), "hit the sack" (go to bed), "hit the roof" (become very angry).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Decapitate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Behead.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Decapitate" is a verb meaning to cut off the head of a person or animal. (सिर काटना)

• "Behead" carries exactly the same meaning, so it is the correct synonym.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Affection" means fondness or love. (स्नेह)

• Option 2 "Sincerity" means honesty of mind, freedom from pretence. (ईमानदारी)

• Option 3 "Desolation" means a state of bleak emptiness or misery. (उजाड़, वीरानी)

NOTE

• Root: Latin de- (off) + caput (head). The same root gives capital (punishment involving the head/life), captain (head of a team) and per capita (per head).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

It takes two to tango
option_1: Two people are required for a couple dance
option_3: For an argument both parties are equally responsible
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. For an argument both parties are equally responsible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "It takes two to tango" means that when two people are involved in a quarrel or a wrongdoing, both share the responsibility — one side alone cannot be blamed. (ताली दोनों हाथों से बजती है)

◦ Example: You cannot blame only your brother for the fight; it takes two to tango.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 gives the literal meaning of the tango dance, not the idiomatic meaning — an idiom is never taken literally.

• Option 2 "To fight fiercely" matches idioms like "to be at daggers drawn".

• Option 4 "An interesting idea" has no connection with the idiom.

NOTE

• The exact Hindi equivalent is "ताली एक हाथ से नहीं बजती". Similar English idioms of shared blame: "two of a kind", "birds of a feather".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Fetal ______ screening uses ultrasound scanning to find certain abnormalities in the baby.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. anomaly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Anomaly" means something that deviates from the normal; an irregularity or abnormality. (असामान्यता)

• "Fetal anomaly screening" is the standard medical term for the ultrasound scan done to detect abnormalities in the unborn baby — and the sentence itself defines it as finding "certain abnormalities".

◦ Correct: Fetal anomaly screening uses ultrasound scanning to find certain abnormalities in the baby.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "enfevering" (causing fever) is not the term used with screening and does not suit the context.

• Option 3 "abeyance" means a state of temporary suspension ("the matter is in abeyance"). (स्थगन)

• Option 4 "snuggle" means to nestle closely for warmth or affection — irrelevant here.

NOTE

• Note the repeated clue "abnormalities" in the sentence; the blank must echo it. Synonyms of anomaly: irregularity, aberration, deviation, oddity.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

For years, people afflicted with the itchy skin condition used stinky coal tar derivatives to _______ their symptoms.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. alleviate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Alleviate" means to make (pain, suffering or a problem) less severe; to relieve. (कम करना, राहत देना)

• People with an itchy skin condition would use coal tar preparations to relieve/ease their symptoms, so "alleviate" is the natural collocation: alleviate pain / symptoms / suffering.

◦ Correct: ... used stinky coal tar derivatives to alleviate their symptoms.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "obviate" means to remove a difficulty in advance so that it never arises; symptoms already present can be relieved, not obviated.

• Option 2 "refer" means to direct attention to, or send someone to a specialist — it needs "to" and changes the meaning.

• Option 3 "deviate" means to depart from a course or standard — meaningless with "symptoms".

NOTE

• Learn the pair: alleviate (lighten, from Latin levis = light) vs aggravate (make worse). Other words from levis: levity, elevate, relieve.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

(No sooner had the ink dried on last week's column, that) one of my long-suffering 17 readers was into action.
option_1: No sooner had the ink dry on last week's column, than
option_2: No sooner did the ink dried on last week's column, than
option_4: No sooner had the ink dried on last week's column, than
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No sooner had the ink dried on last week's column, than.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "No sooner ... than" is a fixed pair. "No sooner" is never followed by "that" or "when"; it must be followed by "than".

• "No sooner" at the beginning of a sentence causes inversion: No sooner + had + subject + V3 (past participle). Hence "had the ink dried" (dry – dried – dried).

◦ Correct: No sooner had the ink dried on last week's column, than one of my long-suffering readers was into action.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 wrongly uses the base form "dry" after "had" instead of the past participle "dried".

• Option 2 wrongly uses "did ... dried" — after the auxiliary "did" the base form is needed, and the inverted past perfect is the required structure anyway.

• Option 3 "No substitution required" is wrong because the printed segment uses "that" in place of "than".

NOTE

• Other inversion structures for SSC: "Hardly/Scarcely had ... when", "Barely had ... when", "Not only ... but also", "Seldom/Rarely/Never had ...".

question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

The (captain with the members of his team) failed to qualify for the African Nations Cup finals.
option_3: captain along with the members of his team
option_4: captain along side the members of his team
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. captain and his team.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sense intended is that the whole side — the captain together with his players — failed to qualify. To make them jointly the subject of the plural verb "failed", they must be joined by the conjunction "and", which creates a genuine plural subject.

• "captain and his team" is also the most concise and idiomatic way of expressing this.

◦ Correct: The captain and his team failed to qualify for the African Nations Cup finals.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "No correction required" is wrong: with the prepositional phrase "with the members of his team", the team is only a parenthetical addition, so the sentence reads as though the captain alone failed — not the intended meaning.

• Option 3 "captain along with the members of his team" has the same defect and is needlessly wordy.

• Option 4 is doubly wrong — "along side" should be written as one word, "alongside".

NOTE

• Remember the agreement rule: phrases like with, along with, together with, as well as, besides, in addition to do not change the number of the subject. "The captain, along with his players, was present." Only "and" makes a compound plural subject.

question: Select the correctly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Definition.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "DEFINITION" — DE + FI + NI + TION. It means a statement of the exact meaning of a word or the nature of something. (परिभाषा)

• Note that the vowel before "-tion" is i, not a: definition.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Deifinatn" — letters transposed and the ending mutilated.

• Option 2 "Defination" — a very common error; there is no "a" in the third syllable.

• Option 4 "Definasion" — the "-sion" ending is wrong; the word takes "-tion".

NOTE

• Word family: define (verb), definition (noun), definite (adjective), definitely (adverb), definitive (final, authoritative). Beware of the frequent misspellings "definately" and "defination".

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Your success were short-lived and had disastrous outcomes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Your success were.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Success" here is an uncountable/singular noun, so it must take the singular verb "was", not the plural "were".

◦ Correct: Your success was short-lived and had disastrous outcomes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "short-lived and" is correctly formed — "short-lived" is a compound adjective meaning lasting only a brief time.

• "had disastrous outcomes." is correct; the past tense "had" matches the past-tense narration.

• "No error" cannot be selected because the subject-verb agreement is clearly faulty.

NOTE

• Subject-verb agreement: singular subject → singular verb (is/was/has), plural subject → plural verb (are/were/have). Uncountable nouns such as success, information, advice, furniture, luggage, news, equipment always take a singular verb.

question: Select the wrongly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. expereince.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word is misspelt; the correct spelling is "experience" — EX + PE + RI + ENCE. It means knowledge or skill gained by doing something, or an event one lives through. (अनुभव)

• The printed form "expereince" wrongly transposes "ri" into "re".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "enigma" (correctly spelt) means a mystery or a puzzling person/thing. (पहेली)

• Option 3 "equivocate" (correctly spelt) means to use ambiguous language so as to conceal the truth. (गोलमोल बात करना)

• Option 4 "effigy" (correctly spelt) means a model or dummy of a person, often burnt in protest. (पुतला)

NOTE

• In a "wrongly spelt word" question, check every option letter by letter; three will be perfect and only one will be flawed. Related spelling traps: experiment, experience, experiential, expertise.

question:
Select the word from the options which is similar in meaning to the bracketed part given in the sentence below.

He has been used as the (fall guy) for issues with housing and unemployment.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. scapegoat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "fall guy" is a person who is made to take the blame for someone else's mistake or crime. The exact one-word equivalent is "scapegoat". (बलि का बकरा)

◦ Correct: He has been used as the scapegoat for issues with housing and unemployment.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "reticent" means reserved, unwilling to speak. (अल्पभाषी)

• Option 2 "confiscate" is a verb meaning to seize property officially. (ज़ब्त करना)

• Option 4 "weakling" means a physically or morally weak person — being blamed is not the same as being weak.

NOTE

• The word "scapegoat" comes from the Biblical goat symbolically loaded with the sins of the people and driven into the wilderness. Related expressions: "take the rap", "carry the can", "whipping boy".

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

The kids there were so notorious, the / more I asked them to quiet down, / the more loud they would scream.
option_2: the more loud they would scream.
option_3: more I asked them to quiet down,
option_4: The kids there were so notorious, the
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. the more loud they would scream.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence uses the double comparative structure "the more ... the more ...". In this structure a one-syllable adjective such as "loud" forms its comparative with -er, not with "more".

• Hence "the more loud" is wrong; it must be "the louder".

◦ Correct: ... the more I asked them to quiet down, the louder they would scream.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "The kids there were so notorious, the" is acceptable as printed in this segment-wise question.

• "more I asked them to quiet down," is correct — "more" here modifies the verb phrase, and "the more I asked" is the standard first half of the structure.

• "No error" cannot be chosen since "more loud" violates the comparative rule.

NOTE

• Comparative formation: one-syllable adjectives take -er/-est (loud – louder – loudest; tall – taller – tallest); adjectives of three or more syllables take more/most (beautiful – more beautiful). Never write "more louder" or "more loud".

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

In exactly the same words as were used originally
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Verbatim.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Verbatim" means word for word; in exactly the same words as were originally used. (शब्दशः)

◦ Example: The reporter quoted the minister verbatim.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Misanthrope" — a person who hates or distrusts mankind. (मानव-द्वेषी)

• Option 3 "Kennel" — a shelter or house for a dog.

• Option 4 "Lunatic" — a person who is mentally ill or wildly foolish.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions frequently asked: Verbose (using more words than needed), Verbatim (word for word), Verbal (relating to words), Plagiarism (copying another's work as one's own).

question:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Humble
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Assertive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Humble" means modest, having a low opinion of one's own importance; not proud. (विनम्र)

• "Assertive" means confident and forceful in stating one's views or claims — the clear opposite of humble/self-effacing. (दृढ़तापूर्वक अपनी बात रखने वाला)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Votary" means a devoted follower or worshipper of a cause. (अनुयायी)

• Option 2 "Passive" means accepting what happens without active response — closer to humble than opposed to it.

• Option 3 "Diffident" means shy and lacking self-confidence — a synonym of humble, not an antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of humble: modest, meek, unassuming, unpretentious. Antonyms: arrogant, haughty, proud, assertive, conceited, pompous.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Unadulterated and unabashed were/ the two words that the judge use/ to define his performance.
option_2: the two words that the judge use
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. the two words that the judge use.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is in the past tense (see the verb "were" in the first segment), so the relative clause must also be in the past: "the judge used".

• Additionally, with the singular subject "the judge", the present form would have to be "uses"; the bare form "use" is wrong on both counts.

◦ Correct: Unadulterated and unabashed were the two words that the judge used to define his performance.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Unadulterated and unabashed were" is correct — an inverted structure in which the complement comes first and the plural verb "were" agrees with "the two words".

• "to define his performance." is a correct infinitive of purpose.

• "No error" cannot be chosen because of the faulty verb "use".

NOTE

• Rule of sequence of tenses: if the principal clause is in the past tense, the subordinate clause normally takes a past tense too.

• Meanings: unadulterated = pure, unmixed; unabashed = not embarrassed, unashamed.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

An adventurous or bold person
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Foolhardy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Foolhardy" describes a person who is recklessly bold or daring, taking risks without thinking of the danger. (दुस्साहसी)

• Among the given options it is the only word that carries the idea of adventurous/bold behaviour.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Judgemental" means excessively critical of others. (आलोचनात्मक)

• Option 3 "Debonair" means confident, stylish and charming in manner — it refers to elegance, not daring. (सुरुचिपूर्ण)

• Option 4 "Assaultive" means inclined to attack physically — aggressive, not adventurous.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions: Audacious (daring), Intrepid (fearless), Timid/Coward (lacking courage), Daredevil (a recklessly daring person).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Snail slime is made (1)_______ a mixture of substances. It is mostly water (2)_______ with proteins and some carbohydrates and minerals, (3)_______ into a sort of jelly. This jelly is (4)_______ “mucus”. It’s not that different to the snot that comes out of your nose when you have a (5)_______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed expression is "made of", used to say what material or substances a thing consists of.

◦ Correct: Snail slime is made of a mixture of substances.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "made for" means produced for somebody's use, which does not fit before "a mixture of substances".

• Option 3 "made up" would need "of" after it ("made up of"); "made up a mixture" changes the sense to inventing something.

• Option 4 "made upon" is not an English collocation.

NOTE

• Distinguish: made of (material still recognisable — a table made of wood), made from (material changed in form — paper made from wood), made with (ingredients — a cake made with butter), made in (place of manufacture).

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Snail slime is made (1)_______ a mixture of substances. It is mostly water (2)_______ with proteins and some carbohydrates and minerals, (3)_______ into a sort of jelly. This jelly is (4)_______ “mucus”. It’s not that different to the snot that comes out of your nose when you have a (5)_______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. mixed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is followed by the preposition "with", and the collocation "mixed with" means combined or blended with. Water combined with proteins and minerals is naturally "mixed with" them.

◦ Correct: It is mostly water mixed with proteins and some carbohydrates and minerals.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "sliced" and 2 "diced" mean cutting solid food into slices or cubes — impossible for water.

• Option 4 "rotated" means turned around an axis, or alternated in a sequence — irrelevant to a liquid mixture.

NOTE

• Useful collocations with "mix": mix with, mix up (confuse), mixture of, mixed feelings. In a cloze test, always read the word after the blank — here "with" itself points to the answer.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Snail slime is made (1)_______ a mixture of substances. It is mostly water (2)_______ with proteins and some carbohydrates and minerals, (3)_______ into a sort of jelly. This jelly is (4)_______ “mucus”. It’s not that different to the snot that comes out of your nose when you have a (5)_______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. formed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Formed into" means shaped or made into a particular form. The watery mixture takes the shape of a jelly, so it is "formed into a sort of jelly".

◦ Correct: ... water mixed with proteins and some carbohydrates and minerals, formed into a sort of jelly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "moved into" means shifting to a place — it does not describe a change of substance.

• Option 2 "framed into" is not idiomatic; "frame" means to put in a frame or to falsely incriminate.

• Option 3 "tamed" means to domesticate a wild animal — impossible for a chemical mixture.

NOTE

• Collocation: form into, turn into, transform into, convert into, shape into — all express a change of state or shape.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Snail slime is made (1)_______ a mixture of substances. It is mostly water (2)_______ with proteins and some carbohydrates and minerals, (3)_______ into a sort of jelly. This jelly is (4)_______ “mucus”. It’s not that different to the snot that comes out of your nose when you have a (5)_______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. called.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When a name is given to something, the passive structure is "is called + name". The jelly's name is "mucus", so the sentence reads "This jelly is called 'mucus'".

◦ Correct: This jelly is called "mucus".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "hailed" means greeted enthusiastically or acclaimed ("hailed as a hero") — it needs "as" and expresses praise.

• Option 3 "deemed" means considered or judged to be, and is normally followed by an adjective ("deemed necessary"), not by a simple name in quotation marks.

• Option 4 "stepped" is completely unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Naming structures: "It is called X", "It is known as X", "It is termed X", "They call it X". In a cloze, punctuation clues (here the quotation marks around "mucus") often reveal the answer.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

Snail slime is made (1)_______ a mixture of substances. It is mostly water (2)_______ with proteins and some carbohydrates and minerals, (3)_______ into a sort of jelly. This jelly is (4)_______ “mucus”. It’s not that different to the snot that comes out of your nose when you have a (5)_______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. cold.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage speaks of "the snot that comes out of your nose", and the illness that produces a runny nose is a common cold. The standard collocation is "to have a cold".

◦ Correct: It's not that different to the snot that comes out of your nose when you have a cold.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "plague" is a deadly epidemic disease spread by fleas/rats — far too severe and not linked to a running nose.

• Option 3 "bug" is informal for a minor infection but does not specifically cause nasal mucus, and the context clearly points to the cold.

• Option 4 "complaint" means an ailment in general; it is vague and does not explain the running nose.

NOTE

• Health collocations: have a cold, catch a cold, have a headache, have a fever, suffer from flu. Note "a cold" takes the article, while "flu" usually takes "the" — "he has the flu".

question: Annie Besant was associated with which of the following socio-religious movement?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Theosophical Society.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Annie Besant (1847-1933), an Irish-born social reformer, was closely associated with the Theosophical Society, becoming its President in 1907 and making Adyar (Chennai) its international headquarters. (थियोसोफिकल सोसाइटी)

• The Theosophical Society was founded in New York in 1875 by Madame H. P. Blavatsky and Colonel H. S. Olcott; it shifted to India in 1882.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Annie Besant started the Home Rule Movement (1916) at Madras, published the newspapers New India and Commonweal, and in 1917 became the first woman President of the Indian National Congress (Calcutta session).

• She founded the Central Hindu College, Banaras (1898), which later grew into the Banaras Hindu University.

• Option 1 Indian Reform Association was founded by Keshub Chandra Sen (1870); Option 2 Tattvabodhini Sabha by Debendranath Tagore (1839); Option 3 Adi Brahmo Samaj was the branch led by Debendranath Tagore after the 1866 split of the Brahmo Samaj.

NOTE

• Theosophy preached universal brotherhood, the study of ancient religions and the exploration of the hidden laws of nature; it gave Indians pride in their own culture during the national awakening.

question: Air ______ on heating and ______ on cooling.
solution_text:
The correct answer is expands, contracts.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• On heating, the molecules of air gain kinetic energy, move faster and farther apart, so the air expands; on cooling the molecules slow down and come closer, so the air contracts. (गर्म करने पर फैलती है, ठंडा करने पर सिकुड़ती है)

• This is the phenomenon of thermal expansion, and gases show the greatest expansion, followed by liquids and then solids.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Charles's Law: at constant pressure, the volume of a fixed mass of gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature (V ∝ T).

• Hot air being less dense rises — this principle is used in hot-air balloons, in chimneys and in the formation of land and sea breezes.

• Anomalous expansion of water: water contracts on heating from 0°C to 4°C and expands after 4°C, so ice floats and aquatic life survives in winter.

NOTE

• Other gas laws: Boyle's Law (P ∝ 1/V at constant T), Gay-Lussac's Law (P ∝ T at constant V), and the combined Ideal Gas Equation PV = nRT.

question: Who among the following Mughal Emperors had assumed the title of Padshah?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Babur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Babur (1483-1530), the founder of the Mughal Empire in India, assumed the title "Padshah" (Emperor) in 1507 at Kabul, discarding the older Timurid title "Mirza". (बाबर — पादशाह की उपाधि)

• He defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat (1526), laying the foundation of Mughal rule in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Babur's other major battles: Khanwa (1527) against Rana Sanga, Chanderi (1528) against Medini Rai, and Ghaghra (1529) against the Afghans.

• He wrote his memoirs, the Baburnama (Tuzuk-i-Baburi), in Chaghatai Turkish; it was later translated into Persian by Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan.

• Order of the Mughals: Babur → Humayun → Akbar → Jahangir → Shah Jahan → Aurangzeb.

NOTE

• Babur introduced the use of gunpowder artillery and the Tulughma (flanking) and Araba (cart) war tactics in Indian warfare.

question: Garo tribe is related with which region of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is North-eastern.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Garo tribe belongs to the North-eastern region of India, mainly inhabiting the Garo Hills of Meghalaya, with populations also in Assam, Tripura and Nagaland. (गारो जनजाति — पूर्वोत्तर भारत)

• The Garos call themselves A·chik Mande ("hill people") and follow a matrilineal system of inheritance, like the Khasis and Jaintias.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Major festival of the Garos: Wangala, the "Hundred Drums" harvest festival dedicated to the sun god Misi Saljong.

• Meghalaya's three main tribes are the Garo, Khasi and Jaintia; the state's name means "the abode of clouds".

• The Nokrek Biosphere Reserve (a UNESCO reserve) and Balpakram National Park lie in the Garo Hills.

NOTE

• Other North-eastern tribes: Naga, Mizo, Bodo, Apatani, Nyishi, Angami, Bhutia, Tripuri. In the Garo matrilineal system, the youngest daughter (Nokna) inherits the family property.

question: Mohiniattam is a classical dance of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form of Kerala. The name comes from "Mohini", the enchantress avatar of Lord Vishnu, and "attam" meaning dance. (मोहिनीअट्टम — केरल)

• It is a graceful, lasya-style solo dance performed mainly by women, in a plain off-white (kasavu) sari with a gold border, with gentle swaying body movements.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kerala's other classical/traditional forms: Kathakali, Koodiyattam (UNESCO Intangible Heritage), Theyyam and Ottamthullal.

• Famous exponents of Mohiniyattam: Kalyanikutty Amma (called the "mother of Mohiniyattam"), Sunanda Nair, Bharati Shivaji.

• The eight classical dances recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

NOTE

• The classical dances derive their grammar from the Natya Shastra of Bharata Muni. Mohiniyattam uses Sopana style music and lyrics in Manipravalam (a blend of Sanskrit and Malayalam).

question: How often are the Winter Olympic games held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Every four years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Winter Olympic Games are held once every four years (a period called an Olympiad cycle), just like the Summer Olympics. (हर चार वर्ष में)

• Since 1994 the Winter Games have been staggered to fall two years apart from the Summer Games, so an Olympic event occurs every second year.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The first Winter Olympics were held at Chamonix, France, in 1924.

• The 2022 Winter Olympics were held in Beijing, China, making Beijing the first city to host both Summer (2008) and Winter Games; the 2026 edition is scheduled for Milan-Cortina, Italy.

• Winter sports include skiing, ice hockey, figure skating, speed skating, bobsleigh, curling and the biathlon.

NOTE

• The Olympics are organised by the International Olympic Committee (IOC), founded by Baron Pierre de Coubertin in 1894; headquarters at Lausanne, Switzerland. Motto: "Citius, Altius, Fortius - Communiter" (Faster, Higher, Stronger - Together).

question: Which of the following is a characteristic of a plant cell?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cell wall is present.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A plant cell is enclosed by a rigid cell wall made of cellulose, lying outside the plasma membrane. It gives the cell shape, rigidity and protection and prevents bursting in a hypotonic medium. (कोशिका भित्ति)

• Animal cells lack a cell wall, which is the classic distinguishing feature between the two.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is wrong because plant cells have a large central vacuole (often occupying 80-90% of the cell volume), while animal cells have small vacuoles.

• Options 2 and 3 are wrong because plant cells do contain plastids, including green chloroplasts with chlorophyll for photosynthesis.

• Centrioles are typically present in animal cells and absent in most higher plant cells.

NOTE

• Cell wall composition: cellulose in plants, chitin in fungi, peptidoglycan (murein) in bacteria. The cell was discovered by Robert Hooke (1665); Leeuwenhoek first saw living cells; the Cell Theory was given by Schleiden and Schwann (1838-39).

question: Goods which are of durable character which are used in the production process are called _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is capital goods.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Capital goods are durable (long-lasting) goods used in the process of production — machines, tools, plant, equipment and buildings. They are not consumed directly but help produce other goods. (पूँजीगत वस्तुएँ)

• They form part of Gross Fixed Capital Formation and depreciate over time, which is why economists deduct depreciation from GDP to obtain NDP.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 Veblen goods are luxury items (like designer bags) whose demand rises as price rises because of snob value — an exception to the law of demand, named after Thorstein Veblen.

• Option 3 Consumption goods (consumer goods) directly satisfy human wants — food, clothes, television sets.

• Option 4 Complementary goods are used together, so demand for one raises demand for the other — car and petrol, pen and ink.

NOTE

• Other exceptions to the law of demand: Giffen goods (inferior goods whose demand rises with price), goods bought for speculation, and goods bought in emergencies.

question: What was the title given to the late Sarojini Naidu?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nightingale of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sarojini Naidu (1879-1949) was popularly called the "Nightingale of India" (Bharat Kokila) because of her lyrical, melodious poetry. (भारत कोकिला)

• She was the first Indian woman President of the Indian National Congress (Kanpur session, 1925) and the first woman Governor of an Indian state (United Provinces, 1947).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Her famous poetry collections: The Golden Threshold (1905), The Bird of Time (1912) and The Broken Wing (1917).

• She took a leading part in the Non-Cooperation Movement, the Salt Satyagraha (Dharasana Satyagraha, 1930) and the Quit India Movement.

• Her birthday, 13 February, is observed as National Women's Day in India.

NOTE

• Other well-known titles: Annie Besant - "Mother of Indian Home Rule"; Rabindranath Tagore - "Gurudev"; Subhas Chandra Bose - "Netaji"; Lata Mangeshkar - "Nightingale of Bollywood".

question: Who appoints the Chief Justice of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is President.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Chief Justice of India (CJI) and other judges of the Supreme Court are appointed by the President of India under Article 124(2) of the Constitution. (राष्ट्रपति द्वारा नियुक्ति)

• By convention, the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court is appointed CJI; appointments are made on the recommendation of the Collegium (CJI + four senior-most judges).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Qualifications for a Supreme Court judge: citizen of India, and either a High Court judge for 5 years, or an advocate of a High Court for 10 years, or a distinguished jurist in the President's opinion.

• Retirement age: 65 years for Supreme Court judges and 62 years for High Court judges.

• A judge can be removed by the President only after an address by both Houses of Parliament supported by a special majority, on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity (Article 124(4)).

NOTE

• The Supreme Court was inaugurated on 28 January 1950; its first CJI was Justice H. J. Kania. The 99th Constitutional Amendment creating the NJAC was struck down by the Supreme Court in 2015, restoring the Collegium system.

question: Which of the following is a fundamental duty stated under the Indian constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is To defend the country.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 51A(d) of the Constitution lays down the Fundamental Duty "to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so". (देश की रक्षा करना)

• Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, and are contained in Part IV-A, Article 51A.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Originally 10 duties were added; the 86th Amendment (2002) added the 11th — for a parent/guardian to provide education to a child between 6 and 14 years.

• Other duties include: abiding by the Constitution and respecting the National Flag and National Anthem, cherishing the ideals of the freedom struggle, promoting harmony, protecting the environment, developing scientific temper, and safeguarding public property.

• Note that the duty is to safeguard public property (Option 1 wrongly says private property) and to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women — not a general duty "to protect dignity".

NOTE

• Fundamental Duties, like the Directive Principles, are non-justiciable — they cannot be enforced by the courts. The idea was borrowed from the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

question: Breeding of fish in specially constructed tanks and ponds is called _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pisciculture.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pisciculture (fish farming) is the rearing and breeding of fish in specially constructed tanks, ponds and enclosures for commercial purposes. (मत्स्य पालन)

• It is a branch of aquaculture, and India is among the world's largest fish producers.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Viticulture — cultivation of grapes. (Related: viniculture = wine production.)

• Option 2 Horticulture — cultivation of fruits, vegetables, flowers and ornamental plants.

• Option 4 Sericulture — rearing of silkworms for silk production.

NOTE

• Other "-culture" terms for SSC: Apiculture (bees/honey), Aquaculture (aquatic organisms), Floriculture (flowers), Olericulture (vegetables), Silviculture (forest trees), Vermiculture (earthworms), Moriculture (mulberry).

• The Blue Revolution in India refers to the rapid growth of fish and aquaculture production; the PM Matsya Sampada Yojana (2020) promotes it.

question: Ritusamhara or The Six Seasons is a classic of Sanskrit literature, written by _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalidasa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ritusamhara" ("The Medley/Gathering of Seasons", or The Six Seasons) is an early lyrical poem (khanda-kavya) by Kalidasa, describing the six Indian seasons and their effect on lovers. (कालिदास — ऋतुसंहार)

• Kalidasa is regarded as the greatest poet-dramatist of classical Sanskrit and is traditionally placed in the court of Chandragupta II 'Vikramaditya' of the Gupta period.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other works of Kalidasa: plays Abhijnanashakuntalam, Malavikagnimitram, Vikramorvashiyam; poems Meghaduta, Raghuvamsha, Kumarasambhava.

• Option 1 Tulsidas wrote the Ramcharitmanas in Awadhi. Option 2 Ravi Kirti composed the Aihole inscription of the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II. Option 4 Harisena was the court poet of Samudragupta and wrote the Allahabad (Prayag) Prashasti.

NOTE

• The six Indian seasons described are Grishma (summer), Varsha (monsoon), Sharad (autumn), Hemanta (pre-winter), Shishira (winter) and Vasanta (spring).

question: ENSO is the phenomenon related to pressure conditions. What is the full form of ENSO?
solution_text:
The correct answer is El Nino Southern Oscillation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• ENSO stands for "El Nino Southern Oscillation" — the coupled ocean-atmosphere phenomenon involving the periodic warming of the eastern Pacific (El Nino) and the see-saw of atmospheric pressure between Tahiti and Darwin (Southern Oscillation). (अल नीनो दक्षिणी दोलन)

• The Southern Oscillation was discovered by Sir Gilbert Walker, who linked Pacific pressure changes with the failure of the Indian monsoon.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• El Nino ("the little boy" in Spanish) brings warm waters off Peru, weakens the trade winds and is usually associated with weak/deficient monsoon rainfall in India and drought in Australia.

• La Nina ("the little girl") is the opposite, cold phase and generally brings a good monsoon to India.

• The index used to measure the pressure see-saw is the Southern Oscillation Index (SOI).

NOTE

• Another important Indian Ocean phenomenon is the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD); a positive IOD can offset the negative effect of El Nino on the Indian monsoon.

question: Bhakra Nangal dam is built on which of the following river?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sutlej.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bhakra Nangal Dam is built on the river Sutlej at Bhakra village in Bilaspur district, Himachal Pradesh, near the Punjab border. (सतलुज नदी)

• It is a concrete gravity dam about 226 metres high, one of the highest in the world of its kind; the reservoir it creates is called the Govind Sagar (named after Guru Gobind Singh).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Bhakra Nangal project is a joint venture of Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan; Jawaharlal Nehru called such projects the "temples of modern India".

• Other dams: Pong Dam on the Beas, Thein (Ranjit Sagar) Dam on the Ravi, Salal and Baglihar on the Chenab, Tehri on the Bhagirathi, Sardar Sarovar on the Narmada, Hirakud on the Mahanadi (longest earthen dam).

• Under the Indus Waters Treaty (1960), India has full rights over the eastern rivers Ravi, Beas and Sutlej, while Pakistan uses the western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab.

NOTE

• The Sutlej rises from Rakas Tal near Mansarovar in Tibet and enters India through the Shipki La pass in Himachal Pradesh.

question: Who among the following became the first Indian player to score 1,000 T20 International runs in a calendar year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Suryakumar Yadav.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Suryakumar Yadav became the first Indian batter to score 1,000 runs in T20 Internationals in a single calendar year, achieving the feat in 2022. (सूर्यकुमार यादव)

• He was only the second batter in the world to do so, after Mohammad Rizwan of Pakistan (2021).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• For his outstanding 2022 season, Suryakumar Yadav was named the ICC Men's T20I Cricketer of the Year 2022, an honour he retained in 2023.

• Known as "Mr 360" for his ability to score all around the wicket, he topped the ICC T20I batting rankings.

• Virat Kohli holds the record for the most runs in T20 World Cups and was Player of the Tournament in 2014 and 2016.

NOTE

• T20 International cricket began in 2005 (Australia vs New Zealand); India won the inaugural ICC World T20 in 2007 under MS Dhoni and again in 2024 under Rohit Sharma.

question: _______ unemployment refers to the lowest unemployment level a healthy economy can sustain without causing inflation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Natural.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The natural rate of unemployment is the lowest level of unemployment that a healthy economy can sustain without causing inflation. It corresponds to full employment and consists of frictional plus structural unemployment. (प्राकृतिक बेरोज़गारी)

• It is also called the NAIRU — the Non-Accelerating Inflation Rate of Unemployment — a concept associated with Milton Friedman and Edmund Phelps.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Structural unemployment arises from a mismatch between workers' skills and the jobs available, caused by technological or industrial change.

• Disguised unemployment occurs when more people are employed than actually needed, so the marginal productivity of the extra workers is nearly zero — common in Indian agriculture.

• Frictional unemployment is the short-term joblessness while people move between jobs or enter the labour force.

NOTE

• Other types: Cyclical (due to a recession), Seasonal (agriculture, tourism), Educated and Open unemployment. Unemployment data in India is collected through the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) by the NSO.

question: In Indus valley civilization, the city of Lothal stood beside a tributary of the _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sabarmati.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lothal, the famous Harappan port town in Gujarat (Ahmedabad district), was situated on the Bhogava river, a tributary of the Sabarmati, near the Gulf of Khambhat. (साबरमती की सहायक नदी)

• Lothal is best known for its dockyard, the earliest known artificial dock in the world, used for berthing and servicing ships.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Lothal was excavated by S. R. Rao (1955-1962). Other finds: a bead-making factory, a Persian Gulf seal, rice husk, a fire altar and a terracotta figure of a horse.

• Other Harappan sites and rivers: Harappa on the Ravi, Mohenjo-daro on the Indus, Kalibangan on the Ghaggar, Ropar on the Sutlej, Dholavira on the Khadir Beyt (Rann of Kutch), Banawali on the Saraswati.

• Dholavira (Gujarat) was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021.

NOTE

• The Indus Valley (Harappan) Civilization was a Bronze Age civilization (c. 2500-1750 BCE), discovered in 1921 by Daya Ram Sahni at Harappa and in 1922 by R. D. Banerji at Mohenjo-daro.

question: Under the Atal Pension Yojana, the pension returns are given after the subscriber turns ______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is 60.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under the Atal Pension Yojana (APY), the guaranteed monthly pension begins after the subscriber attains the age of 60 years. (60 वर्ष की आयु के बाद)

• Subscribers receive a guaranteed minimum pension of Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000 per month, depending on the contribution made; the same pension is payable to the spouse after the subscriber's death, and the accumulated corpus is returned to the nominee thereafter.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• APY was launched on 9 May 2015 and is administered by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA).

• Eligibility: any Indian citizen aged 18-40 years with a savings bank account; contributions must therefore be made for at least 20 years.

• It replaced the earlier Swavalamban Yojana and mainly targets workers in the unorganised sector.

NOTE

• Other social security schemes launched in 2015: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (life cover) and Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (accident cover).

question: Who has won the most individual gold Olympic medals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Michael Phelps.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The American swimmer Michael Phelps has won the most individual Olympic gold medals — 13, besides holding the record for the most Olympic medals of all time (28, including 23 golds). (माइकल फेल्प्स)

• He won a record 8 gold medals at a single Games (Beijing 2008), surpassing Mark Spitz's 7 golds of 1972.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Usain Bolt (Jamaica) won 8 Olympic golds in sprinting and is the world record holder in the 100 m (9.58 s) and 200 m (19.19 s).

• Katie Ledecky (USA) is the most decorated female swimmer, and Simone Biles (USA) is the most decorated gymnast in World Championship history.

• Phelps competed in Athens 2004, Beijing 2008, London 2012 and Rio 2016.

NOTE

• The Olympic rings, designed by Pierre de Coubertin (1913), represent the five inhabited continents; the colours blue, yellow, black, green and red on a white field include at least one colour from every national flag.

question: “Gurpurab” is celebrated as a birth anniversary of which Sikh guru?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Guru Nanak Dev.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guru Nanak Gurpurab (also called Guru Nanak Jayanti or Prakash Parv) is celebrated as the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev, the first Sikh Guru and founder of Sikhism. (गुरु नानक देव जी का प्रकाश पर्व)

• It falls on Kartik Purnima (the full-moon day of the month of Kartik), usually in November.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Guru Nanak Dev (1469-1539) was born at Talwandi (now Nankana Sahib, Pakistan); his teachings are summed up as "Naam Japo, Kirat Karo, Vand Chhako".

• The ten Sikh Gurus: Nanak Dev, Angad Dev (developed the Gurmukhi script), Amar Das, Ram Das (founded Amritsar), Arjan Dev (compiled the Adi Granth, built the Harmandir Sahib, first martyr), Hargobind, Har Rai, Har Krishan, Tegh Bahadur, Gobind Singh (founded the Khalsa in 1699 and made the Guru Granth Sahib the eternal Guru).

• Celebrations include Prabhat Pheris, Akhand Path (48-hour continuous reading of the Guru Granth Sahib), Nagar Kirtan and Langar.

NOTE

• The birth anniversary of Guru Gobind Singh is separately observed as Prakash Parv in December/January, and Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom is marked in November.

question: Which of the following states primarily celebrate the chhath puja festival in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chhath Puja is celebrated primarily in Bihar, along with Jharkhand, eastern Uttar Pradesh and Nepal's Terai region. (छठ पूजा — बिहार)

• It is dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and his consort Usha/Chhathi Maiya, and involves offering arghya (water offerings) to the setting and rising sun while standing in a river or pond.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The festival lasts four days: Nahay Khay, Kharna (Lohanda), Sandhya Arghya and Usha Arghya (Paran); devotees keep a rigorous nirjala (waterless) fast of about 36 hours.

• It falls on the sixth day (Shashthi) of the bright fortnight of the month of Kartika, a few days after Diwali; hence the name "Chhath" (six).

• Other state festivals: Bihu (Assam), Pongal (Tamil Nadu), Onam (Kerala), Baisakhi (Punjab), Bathukamma (Telangana), Hornbill Festival (Nagaland).

NOTE

• Chhath is one of the few Hindu festivals with no idol worship and no priestly mediation, and it is notable for its emphasis on cleanliness and environmental purity.

question: Rukmini Devi Arundale was awarded with ‘Padma Bhushan’ in the year _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1956.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rukmini Devi Arundale (1904-1986), the celebrated dancer and revivalist of Bharatanatyam, was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1956. (रुक्मिणी देवी अरुंडेल)

• She founded Kalakshetra at Adyar, Chennai, in 1936, an institution devoted to the revival of classical dance and music.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• She purified and re-established the temple dance form Sadir as the respectable classical art now known as Bharatanatyam, and was the first woman nominated to the Rajya Sabha (1952).

• She was also a noted animal-welfare activist, instrumental in the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960, and was offered the post of President of India, which she declined.

• She received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (1967) as well.

NOTE

• Civilian awards, in order of precedence: Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri; instituted in 1954 and announced on Republic Day.

question: Which among the following acids is found in coconut oil?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lauric Acid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lauric acid (dodecanoic acid, C12) is the principal saturated fatty acid in coconut oil, forming roughly 45-50% of it. (लॉरिक अम्ल — नारियल तेल)

• It is also abundant in palm kernel oil and in human breast milk, and is valued for its antimicrobial properties and for making soaps and detergents.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Erucic acid occurs in mustard and rapeseed oil.

• Option 2 Oxalic acid is found in tomatoes, spinach and other leafy vegetables.

• Option 3 Lactic acid is found in sour milk/curd and accumulates in muscles during vigorous exercise, causing cramps.

NOTE

• Common natural acids: Citric acid (citrus fruits), Malic acid (apples), Tartaric acid (tamarind, grapes), Acetic acid (vinegar), Formic acid (ant sting), Butyric acid (rancid butter), Ascorbic acid (Vitamin C, amla).

question: ______ is a process in which natural rubber is treated with sulphur to make it more durable and elastic.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vulcanisation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vulcanisation is the process of heating natural rubber with sulphur (about 3-5%) so that cross-links form between the polymer chains, making the rubber harder, stronger, more elastic and resistant to heat and abrasion. (वल्कनीकरण)

• The process was discovered by Charles Goodyear in 1839 and is named after Vulcan, the Roman god of fire.

NOTE

• Natural rubber is a polymer of isoprene obtained as latex from the Hevea brasiliensis tree; Kerala is India's largest producer. Vulcanised rubber is used for tyres, hoses, shoe soles and conveyor belts.
